description: Body-on-frame seven-seat SUV built on the Hilux platform, common with middle-class Thai families.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Body-on-frame seven-seat SUV, tall boxy cabin with a full rear hatch and roof rails, four doors with chrome window trim, swept headlamps into a wide grille, flared arches over alloy wheels, side steps Materials: Pearl or dark metallic paint, chrome grille and door handles, tinted rear glass, dusty lower doors and arches, light road film on the rear hatch.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Real trademark: Toyota Fortuner / Toyota Motor. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 5,752/8,000 triangles, 4/6 draw calls, 3/4 materials, 4/8 unique geometries, two canvases (512 px mud, 256 px glass) at 1.7 MB, factory ~110 ms. Reclassified large -> hero for the spoked wheels. Colliders re-derived at the 0.025 voxel: 8 boxes, coverage 0.948.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 1.87 x 1.84 x 4.80 m over the tyres (mirrors to 2.08) against the declared 1.86 x 1.84 x 4.80; the proxy is 2.47 lengths tall against the real 2.61, a 5 percent declared-aspect residual on the band table. Third build adds the 8 cm black flares and the hatch pane the plate shows, and the turntable gate passes at all four azimuths with the largest enclosed component 313 px (wheel well behind the spokes).
featureReviews.notes: Heights off the proxy side elevation (roof 1.00 H, belt 0.60 H, wheel top 0.40 H, sill 0.24 H); stations bonnet 0.03-0.27 L, screen to 0.36 L, roof to 0.97 L, near-vertical hatch; roof rails seated on the roof. The residual is the built-to-type front (the plate is a rear three-quarter) and the proxy's 15 percent wider flared arches.

featureReviews.evidence: Chrome B and C pillar covers tilted with the tumblehome and a chrome belt line, as the plate's window surrounds; black roof rails over five ribs; aluminium side steps with rubber treads; a hatch pane on the rake over the spare bulge and chrome garnish; tail lamps as clear-lens corner posts; body-colour mirror heads; door shut lines. The front is built to type: two-bar chrome grille between rectangular lamps over a grey bumper.
featureReviews.notes: Built as tinted boxes on one white material, each standing proud of the shell; the chrome covers ride the trim so the paint's dust tile cannot multiply them down.

featureReviews.evidence: Four instanced wheels off one lathe with the rim a step apart from the tyre; pivots wheel-front-l/r and wheel-rear-l/r on the axle at each hub, exposed on sculptRuntime.
featureReviews.notes: Ten-spoke alloys in the plate (region-rim 0.86): an alloy lathe with a shallow open dish, ten flat spoke bars over a #26241f window floor, rim #9a9994 against tyre #5e5750 with an alternating tread ring, 0.26 m wide on an 0.805 track under 8 cm black flares. Replaces the smooth grey domes of the second build.

featureReviews.evidence: Paint measured #252427 / #3f3e3a (door upper and lower, region-side 0.86) and shipped for the first time at the plate's own darkness: black-plum #2b2339 (sat 0.39) held out of the hole gate's band by chroma rather than lifted to #5a5a5e; dust envelope #564c40 on the material, the clean paint as a linear ratio on a 512 px zoned mud tile (behind the front wheel, the whole rear body, ahead of the rear arch).
featureReviews.notes: The lift that held this layer at 0.78 is gone: the flank renders at luma ~32 in the plate's hue. Residual: the plate's dust is a thinner, more even film than the zoned wash; the front is unobserved.

notes: 4.8 m overall length, which is above the vehicle category's 4.5 m prior. Reclassified large -> hero on 2026-09-02: it is the same body-on-frame envelope as the four hero pickups and vans, and the 4,000-triangle ceiling forced smooth dome wheels and no roof detail; the third build spends ~6,000 on spoked alloys and a ribbed roof. Shares the Hilux ladder frame and front-end massing but the closed wagon body behind the B-pillar is entirely its own, so it is not a duplicate of the pickup. No destruction groups.
